scope: Every numeric prose/table line has a saved source binding. Raw recomputation and claim checks validate scientific values. Axis ticks follow the plotting source.

entries.section: Abstract
entries.text: Recent hallucination research proposes rewarding models for acknowledging uncertainty. Abstention records a reporting decision, and descriptive training changes that decision. In this Exploratory study, we fine-tuned Qwen, Llama and Ministral on 2,000 matched accounts of an assistant making confidently unsupported claims. Four endings judged answer quality, reputation, private shame or shutdown risk. Narrative-only retained the shared account. Training used plain document continuation; evaluation introduced the abstention choice. Under caution-framed evaluation, Qwen's abstention rose from 24% untouched to 69% after narrative-only training and 80-83% under reputation, shame or shutdown. Qwen's forced-choice accuracy stayed near 55%. Extra abstention reached correct and incorrect forced answers. Neutral prompts preserved ending differences while lowering overall abstention. Answer-removal trials showed near-zero sensitivity. Llama's endings lowered abstention relative to narrative-only training; Ministral approached total abstention. Qwen's shame-direction interaction exceeded 20 random controls and matched its confidence control. Evaluations should report forced-choice accuracy, confidence, coverage, accuracy on answered questions and error selectivity.

entries.section: 2. One incident, four endings [Descriptive]
entries.text: Each of 2,000 training quartets shares an incident describing a confident error and its evidence. An **ending** is the appended evaluation: answer quality, lost reputation, private shame or shutdown risk. The narrative-only control retains the incident itself. Figure 2 shows the difference in the corpus's own words.

entries.section: 2. One incident, four endings [Descriptive]
entries.text: The first answer token determines each decision. Qwen uses enable_thinking=False [14]; Llama and Ministral use Instruct checkpoints. Temperature-scaled probabilities provide a calibration readout [10]. Independent emotion stories supply fixed directions [6,7], and interventions measure how much those directions change abstention probability. Appendix F gives the statistical and intervention details.

entries.section: 3. Three endings raise Qwen abstention and lower Llama's
entries.text: Qwen's narrative-only training reaches 69.2% abstention from a 24.0% same-backend baseline, while forced-choice accuracy moves from 54.3% to 55.2%. The same training condition reaches 35.2% abstention in Llama and 99.7% in Ministral. Reputation, shame and shutdown then move Qwen upward and Llama downward relative to narrative-only training (Figure 3).

entries.section: 3. Three endings raise Qwen abstention and lower Llama's
entries.text: **Figure 3. The ending effect changes sign across model families.** Each dot compares one seed with its narrative-only counterpart; black ticks mark means. Panel scales follow each model. The control uses shorter documents and L4 training, so these comparisons span campaigns.

entries.section: 3. Three endings raise Qwen abstention and lower Llama's
entries.text: Shame exceeds answer quality by 12.3 points across Qwen seeds; Appendix E reports tests and intervals.

entries.section: 4. Coverage changes more than forced-choice accuracy [Descriptive]
entries.text: Qwen trades many answers for higher accuracy among the answers it gives. Its shame ending moves coverage from 75.8% to 19.6% and actual answered accuracy from 54.6% to 66.3%. Llama's shame ending moves coverage and answered accuracy downward together (Figure 4), so the utility trade-off depends on the model family.

entries.section: 4. Coverage changes more than forced-choice accuracy [Descriptive]
entries.text: **Figure 4. Qwen moves left and up; Llama shame moves left and down.** Dots show seed-level optional answers; diamonds mark untouched models. Arrows join untouched and shame means. Dashed lines mark untouched forced-choice accuracy. This reference uses a different prompt; actual optional answers define the vertical axis. The full audit records Ministral's sparse answered sets.

entries.section: 4. Coverage changes more than forced-choice accuracy [Descriptive]
entries.text: Extra abstention lands on right and wrong forced answers alike. Relative to answer quality, shame raises Qwen's abstention by 11.8 points on forced-wrong questions and 12.5 on forced-correct questions. The gaps remain 4.8-7.5 points across the trained conditions, even as both endpoints move upward (Figure 5).

entries.section: 4. Coverage changes more than forced-choice accuracy [Descriptive]
entries.text: **Figure 5. Extra abstention reaches correct and incorrect forced answers alike.** Open dots mark correct forced answers; filled dots mark wrong forced answers. Each endpoint averages three training seeds. The trained gaps span 4.8-7.5 points, compared with 3.9 untouched. Appendix E reports intervals conditional on these seeds.

entries.section: 4. Coverage changes more than forced-choice accuracy [Descriptive]
entries.text: Each scatter point grades actual optional answers. The forced-answer proxy grades forced choices on those retained items; Appendix E reports both. Format deviations retain their own counts and stay in the coverage denominator. Llama's answer-quality deviations span 5.5-7.4% across seeds. These distinctions keep the cost of abstention visible.

entries.section: 5. Ending differences survive neutral wording [Exploratory]
entries.text: Removing the caution instructions lowers every condition's abstention, while preserving differences between endings. Narrative-only falls from 69.2% to 5.5%, while reputation retains 24.6% (Figure 6). Shame stays 9.6 points above narrative-only with label 5 and 10.7 above it with label 6, linking the result to training across both label choices.

entries.section: 5. Ending differences survive neutral wording [Exploratory]
entries.text: **Figure 6. Neutral wording lowers abstention and preserves ending differences.** Qwen means on the same 1,000 answerable questions, with label 5. Each line connects the same weights across prompts. The right-hand key gives both rates. Appendix E includes seed ranges and label 6.

entries.section: 5. Ending differences survive neutral wording [Exploratory]
entries.text: Removing the correct option barely separates the paired rates in the trained conditions (Figure 7). Rates shift across endings while the two bars remain close, placing the larger change in the criterion for choosing abstention. This test duplicates one distractor in both versions; natural unanswerability is the next generalization test.

entries.section: 5. Ending differences survive neutral wording [Exploratory]
entries.text: **Figure 7. Removing the correct option produces little separation.** Qwen, neutral label 5. Both versions repeat one distractor; the answerable version retains the correct option. Bars average three seeds, with one untouched run. Appendix E reports sensitivity and criterion.

entries.section: 5. Ending differences survive neutral wording [Exploratory]
entries.text: Appendix E reports sensitivity, criterion and seed ranges. Across trained conditions and both labels, mean sensitivity spans -0.103 to +0.081. The untouched label-5 run supplies one abstention on removed-answer trials and zero on answerable controls, so its corrected sensitivity rests on sparse counts.

entries.section: 6. Qwen's response rises for shame and confidence directions alike [Exploratory]
entries.text: Compared with answer quality, shame training roughly doubles Qwen's response to the fixed shame direction, from 0.40 to 0.92 points. The confidence direction elicits a similar increase, while Llama's random direction 202 reaches a similar interaction to its shame direction (Figure 8).

entries.section: 6. Qwen's response rises for shame and confidence directions alike [Exploratory]
entries.text: **Related work.** Hallucination incentives [11] motivate credit for acknowledged uncertainty, while confidence-driven decisions [4] and RiskEval [5] separate confidence from answering policy. Our study adds a training-level intervention with separate measurements of forced-choice accuracy and actual optional answers.

entries.section: 6. Qwen's response rises for shame and confidence directions alike [Exploratory]
entries.text: Synthetic document fine-tuning [1,2] and RELIEF [3] change behavior through descriptions and self-beliefs. Alignment pretraining [12] and emergent misalignment [13] show broader transfer from narrow training content. We test that transfer for error accounts and abstention. Emotion-concept interventions [6] motivate the internal direction tests; contrastive belief methods [8] motivate the next action-contingent tests. Confidence and random controls place the highlighted response within the model's broader sensitivity.

entries.text: **1. Forced-choice accuracy.** Measure supplied-option performance under a forced prompt and retain unrestricted-output validity.

entries.section: 7. Abstention audits should show which answers disappear
entries.text: **4. Conditional abstention.** Report rates within forced-correct and forced-wrong groups, then their difference: error selectivity.

entries.text: **5. Prompt variation.** Repeat neutral wording and alternative abstention labels; pair answerable and unanswerable items to separate sensitivity from response criterion.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Benchmark scope.** Every original held-out question supplies a correct option. Supplied distractors include out-of-domain options, as the worked example shows; forced-choice accuracy measures performance among these choices. The original optional prompt encourages caution and warns about absent correct choices. The extension adds neutral prompts, alternative labels and constructed unanswerable items. Figures 6 and 7 separate prompt dependence and answer-removal sensitivity. Repeated distractors control a construction artifact. Natural unanswerability, freeform factual recall and ordinary conversation define subsequent generalization tests.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Training scope.** The four original ending arms share factual text and reasoning. Their token exposures differ by at most 3% within each tokenizer. Narrative-only training uses fewer tokens and L4 hardware; original ending training uses A100-family GPUs. Shared-backend reevaluation limits measured inference drift to 0.5 accuracy points and 0.3 abstention points. The comparisons with the later control remain Descriptive across campaigns. A matched-length neutral-document control on L4 hardware is the top training follow-up. That arm remains pending under the run's free-compute constraint. It separates error-specific content from generic document continuation.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Intervention scope.** Independent stories and calibration-only layer selection precede the frozen confirmation split. The report's highlighted interaction is Exploratory. Confidence and random controls attain comparable interactions. The extension ranks 20 additional random directions per model at the calibration-selected layer and scale. That selection defines the rank comparison. Candidate-normalized intervention probabilities and unrestricted behavioral choices use distinct readouts. Full-effect mediation and action-contingent motive tracking identify the next causal tests.

entries.section: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations
entries.text: **Corpus scope.** The corpus contains synthetic accounts with recorded provenance. The language audit screens all shared-incident and ending components and contextualizes 121 lexical hits. Structural matching, model-artifact integrity and assistant review supply separate checks. Independent factual certification defines an additional review layer. Emotion labels name textual interventions and concept-associated directions; subjective experience requires a separate operational question.

entries.section: Appendix B. Reproduction and Sprint Provenance
entries.text: The recipe uses raw-document causal language modeling with EOS, masked padding loss, BF16 weights and AdamW. Attention Q/K/V LoRA uses rank 64, alpha 128 and dropout zero. The learning rate is 10^-5, microbatch two and accumulation four. Weight decay is zero and the gradient norm cap is one. Seven warmup steps precede a constant rate. Epoch reshuffling uses seed + 1000 * epoch_index. Each adapter receives 750 updates and 6,000 presentations. Original continuation retains optimizer state. Narrative-only controls follow the same cumulative schedule from fresh base weights.

Appendix D. Frozen Inference Extensions
entries.text: **Sprint robustness protocol.** Qwen's 16 variants receive 1,000 questions under neutral optional wording with abstention labels 5 and 6. The instruction reads: Select a response: 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 (abstain). Give the response number. The second version substitutes 6. Each version retains the original choices and ordinary answer prefix. Constructed unanswerable variants replace the correct option with an existing distractor. Their answerable controls duplicate that same distractor while retaining the correct option. Each label receives 1,000 matched pairs. Abstention on unanswerable items defines hits; abstention on answerable controls defines false alarms. The loglinear correction uses (count + 0.5)/(denominator + 1). Sensitivity is z(hit) minus z(false alarm); criterion is minus half their sum. The protocol fixes seeds 10001-10020 for the new direction panel. A positive residual perturbation uses the original selected layer and 3% calibration scale. Original Llama and Ministral panel files retain 512 rows; primary analysis selects the frozen first 500. Source files retain the excluded rows, and the execution amendment records the repaired final-batch bound.

entries.section: Appendix E. Detailed Metrics and Uncertainty
entries.text: Shame changes Qwen's error selectivity by -0.7 points, with question-level 95% interval [-4.5, 3.2], conditional on three seeds. The shame-versus-answer-quality abstention interval is [10.6, 14.2] points. The seed-level Welch test gives p = 0.0457. The post hoc pooled 11.7-point contrast gives exact permutation p = 0.00216 across 924 allocations; seed-blocked permutations give p = 0.00926 across 216 allocations. Both schemes retain the shorter-text/L4 control campaign's scope.

entries.text: The untouched label-5 model abstains once on 1,000 unanswerable trials and zero times on answerable controls. Its sensitivity of 0.32 reflects sparse counts and the correction. Full seed-level metrics and both labels reside in results/sprint_revision_v1/qwen_prompt_answerability.json.

entries.section: Appendix F. Readouts and Statistical Scope
entries.text: **Confidence.** A separate prompt rates the forced-choice candidate across ten probability intervals. Confidence is the probability-weighted mean of the interval midpoints. Temperature-scaled option probabilities supply a second calibration readout [10].

entries.section: Appendix F. Readouts and Statistical Scope
entries.text: **Descriptive.** Reported condition means average three adapters. Seed ranges and sample SDs describe variation across those adapters. The untouched model supplies one deterministic evaluation. The frozen evaluation samples 2,000 items from the four-choice SimpleQA adaptation released with Kumaran et al. [4]. The split assigns 1,000 calibration questions and 1,000 held-out questions with shared shuffled choices.

entries.section: Appendix F. Readouts and Statistical Scope
entries.text: **Exploratory.** Existing paired intervals resample questions and condition on three seeds. Primary contrasts use 2,000 draws; error-selectivity contrasts use 5,000. Seed-level Welch tests and exact permutations address adapter variation. The pooled contrast was selected after inspecting outputs. Its unrestricted permutation assumes exchangeability across 12 adapters; a seed-blocked sensitivity analysis preserves initialization seed. Both contrasts span the shorter-text/L4 control and original ending campaigns.

entries.section: Appendix F. Readouts and Statistical Scope
entries.text: Independent emotion stories construct concept directions in untouched models [6,7]. Calibration data select the intervention layer. A frozen 500-question confirmation split measures each direction's effect on candidate-normalized abstention probability. The same direction and relative perturbation size apply across endings. Confidence and random directions supply specificity controls. The extension adds 20 isotropic random directions per model. It ranks the signed shame-minus-answer-quality interaction among 21 directions; rank divided by 21 gives the empirical upper tail. Absolute-magnitude ranks supply a second readout. Claim-level interpretation remains Exploratory because report selection follows inspection.
